## India: Regulatory Updates & Implementation

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has confirmed there will be no extensions for Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) compliance deadlines, particularly emphasizing the urgency for startups. This firm stance underscores the government's commitment to the rapid operationalization of the new data protection regime. ([Fortune India](https://news.google.?oc=5))

MeitY has also invited applications for the chairperson and members of the Data Protection Board of India, a critical step towards establishing the independent enforcement body envisioned by the DPDPA. This move signals that the Board is moving closer to becoming fully operational and ready to address data protection grievances and impose penalties. ([Indian Television Dot Com](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiyAFBVV95cUxOaVR4MW9NWUdLSkM5eEVJNFlNeWJBVVRRNzhaU3d0VGdlMlh0V0ExNlNrU2lUdllVMGpYdFFGQ3lIZ1kyOEFIbXNlWks2cHFSX2lTRlB4d1gxY1NDbU1FV3NfRFVYYTB2V29haVpVTEYyWmtDeHFHLURaYnZyaUtlTlptazN3dTc0cVVIajJoenhPTEVCRTFLZjlfVW94OU1YT0U5RWV2VjdZNnJULUlqd1ViM2RBQm02Ti1GTVpWc1hPNnUwZk5XdA?oc=5))

Across government ministries and state bodies, a comprehensive data compliance test is underway to ensure readiness for the DPDPA, highlighting the extensive internal efforts required for public sector adherence. The DPDP Rules 2025 are guiding this transition, with critical compliance deadlines extending into 2026-27 for various entities. ## India: Compliance & Litigation

Despite the advanced stage of DPDPA implementation, many Indian businesses, particularly startups, are reportedly still unprepared for the new data privacy requirements. This highlights a significant gap between regulatory intent and practical readiness on the ground.
